title: Read the timings
description:
Write the helpers of a small benchmarking tool:

```cpp
template <class F> double bestOfMs(F work, int runs);       // runs work() `runs` times; returns the fastest run in milliseconds
double median(std::vector<double> samples);                  // the middle value (the mean of the two middle ones for an even count)
double growthExponent(const std::vector<double>& times);     // times[i] is the time for input size n * 2^i
std::string bigO(double exponent);                           // "O(1)", "O(n)", "O(n^2)", "O(n^3)" or "worse than O(n^3)"
```

- `bestOfMs` times each run with `std::chrono::steady_clock`. `runs` below 1 throws `std::invalid_argument`.
- `median` of an empty vector throws `std::invalid_argument`.
- `growthExponent` estimates `k` in "time grows like nᵏ" from a doubling experiment. Over `m` doublings the time grows by `times.back() / times.front()`, so the average growth per doubling is that ratio to the power `1/m`, and `k` is its base-2 logarithm. It needs at least two times, all greater than 0 (otherwise `std::invalid_argument`).
- `bigO` rounds the exponent to the nearest whole number (`std::lround`): 0 or less gives `O(1)`, 1 `O(n)`, 2 `O(n^2)`, 3 `O(n^3)`, anything bigger `worse than O(n^3)`.
hints: `std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(stop - start).count()` gives the elapsed time as a `double` number of milliseconds.
For `{1, 4, 16}` there are 2 doublings and the time grew 16 times: 16^(1/2) = 4 per doubling, and log₂ 4 = 2, so the code is O(n²).
